query: Which LB sources (LP relaxation, Lagrangian dual, per‑scenario Benders) produce the tightest worst‑case and typical lower bounds for capacitated reliable fixed‑charge facility location?

response.query: Which LB sources (LP relaxation, Lagrangian dual, per‑scenario Benders) produce the tightest worst‑case and typical lower bounds for capacitated reliable fixed‑charge facility location?
response.answer: LP relaxation and Benders decomposition produce tight lower bounds for capacitated reliable fixed-charge facility location. Lagrangian dual is also effective but less commonly used. Per-scenario Benders decomposition can yield tighter bounds in specific scenarios.

In this paper, we propose a novel decomposition approach for mixed-integer stochastic programming (SMIP) problems that is inspired by the combination of penalty-based Lagrangian and block Gauss-Seidel methods (PBGS). In this article, we discuss ways to use these cuts within the framework of Benders’ decomposition algorithms for solving two-stage mixed-binary stochastic problems with binary first-stage variables and continuous recourse. We utilize scenario-based CMIR cuts for TSS-CMIPs and their distributionally robust generalizations with structured CMIPs in the second stage, and prove that these cuts provide conic/linear programming equivalent or approximation for the second stage CMIPs. We also perform extensive computational experiments by solving stochastic and distributionally robust capacitated facility location problem and randomly generated structured TSS-CMIPs with polyhedral CMIPs and second-order CMIPs in the second stage, i.e. p=1 and p=2, respectively. Computational results demonstrate that our proposed method improves the Benders relaxation significantly faster than previous methods for generating Lagrangian cuts and, when used within a branch-and-cut algorithm, significantly reduces the size of the search tree for two classes of test problems. Computational results demonstrate that our proposed method improves the Benders relaxation significantly faster than previous methods for generating Lagrangian cuts and, when used within a branch-and-cut algorithm, significantly reduces the size of the search tree for three classes of test problems. Stochastic-programming models are computationally challenging for large-scale problem instances, and, therefore, we propose a solution technique based on Benders cuts. Our heuristic algorithm demonstrates a significantly improved capacity to handle large-size two-stage problems comparing to three conventional methods for stochastic integer programming, and solving the two-stage model by our heuristic in a rolling horizon provides a good approximation of the multistage problem.
